<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="PubMed-not-MEDLINE" Owner="NLM"><PMID Version="1">38025791</PMID><DateRevised><Year>2023</Year><Month>12</Month><Day>01</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Electronic-eCollection"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">2589-0042</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>26</Volume><Issue>12</Issue><PubDate><Year>2023</Year><Month>Dec</Month><Day>15</Day></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>iScience</Title><ISOAbbreviation>iScience</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Flash-based content addressable memory with L2 distance for memory-augmented neural network.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>108371</StartPage><MedlinePgn>108371</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">108371</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1016/j.isci.2023.108371</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Memory-augmented neural network (MANN) has received increasing attention as a promising approach to achieve lifelong on-device learning, of which implementation of the explicit memory is vital. Content addressable memory (CAM) has been designed to accelerate the explicit memory by harnessing the in-memory-computing capability. In this work, a CAM cell with quadratic code is proposed, and a 1Mb Flash-based multi-bit CAM chip capable of computing Euclidean (L2) distance is fabricated. Compared with ternary CAM, the latency and energy are significantly reduced by 5.3- and 46.6-fold, respectively, for the MANN on Omniglot dataset. Besides, the recognition accuracy has slight degradation (&lt;1%) even after baking for 10<sup>5</sup> s at 200&#xb0;C, demonstrating the robustness to environmental disturbance. Performance evaluation indicates a reduction of 471-fold in latency and 1267-fold in energy compared with GPU for search operation. The proposed robust and energy-efficient CAM provides a promising solution to implement lifelong on-device machine intelligence.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>&#xa9; 2023 The
